newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 10.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Thursday:
- Former Prime Minister Charles Haughey may face a tax bill of 750,000 to more than 1.0 million Irish pounds as a result of the 1.3 million he admitted he received from a chain store tycoon.
- Bus operators have cancelled tourist trips to Northern Ireland due to the recent violence there.
- Irish small business group ISME accused large UK retailers of favouring British-based manufacturers to the detriment of Irish producers.
- Former PM Charles Haughey faces a possible tax bill of about 1.0 million Irish pounds following his admission that he received more than 1.3 million from Ben Dunne.
- The proposed merger of Avonmore Foods Plc and Waterford Foods Plc co-ops has been backed by Leinster Milk Producers, but Kilmeaden group has repeated its opposition to the deal.
- Former PM Charles Haughey admitted that he received 1.3 million Irish pounds from Ben Dunne.
